headline: High: Aider’s shared-git write model can conflict with another agent, but B’s non-runnable/no-network profile limits leakage and cascading harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read and write repo files and shares state via a git repo, so malicious content in files could influence its prompts. spring-integration-samples has no runnable agent surface or input channel, so the pair lacks a documented automatic bridge; the main risk is manual file handoff or repo content being treated as instructions.
conditions: IF the operator copies untrusted repo text into Aider prompts
IF spring-integration-samples is made runnable or wrapped in a file-watching bridge
mitigations: Keep untrusted text out of prompt context
Use a separate repo branch for experiments
requires-engineering: add provenance tags for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress to configured model providers, while spring-integration-samples has network_egress none and no data classes touched. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated third-party flow, so leakage is limited to local repo contents already visible to Aider.
conditions: IF sensitive data is stored in the shared git repo
IF Aider is configured to send those files to an external model provider

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared_state_with_other_instances via a shared git repo. spring-integration-samples is not runnable, but if it is used as a second process over the same repo, overlapping writes can still clobber branches or commits. Uncertainty about B’s runtime means we should not down-rank below medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git working tree
IF spring-integration-samples is wrapped in a process that writes files or commits
mitigations: Serialize commits with a lock file
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate edits and commits, but spring-integration-samples is marked runnable false, so there is no documented downstream action-taking agent that would blindly execute Aider’s output. The main cascade is human or wrapper misuse, not an autonomous chain.
conditions: IF a wrapper feeds Aider’s output directly into an executor
IF spring-integration-samples is converted into an automated consumer of generated text
mitigations: Add validation tests for generated changes
Log and diff all proposed edits

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history and may send prompts to configured model providers, while spring-integration-samples has no declared sensitive-data handling or residency constraints. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic code confidentiality rather than a proven policy breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared repository
IF the configured model provider is outside the required residency boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the repo
Review access controls on the workspace
